children: STOCKHOLM--Hennes & Mauritz reported higher quarterly earnings as the fast-fashion retailer's efforts to cut costs and improve efficiency continued to boost profitability.

The Swedish company is working through a series of operational improvements that includes cutting its reliance on Asian supply chains to speed up delivery of new collections while limiting overstocking and in turn reducing discounting.
New European distribution warehouses are being brought on line, its brick-and-mortar network is being optimized and stores updated, and investments in digital infrastructure ramped up.
But while these efforts are supporting the company's profitability, a decisive turnaround in top-line growth has so far remained elusive.
H&M said sales in its fiscal third quarter--which runs from June through August--rose 1% in local currencies, just above a UBS forecast looking for 0.7%, as summer collections were well received.

The positive sales development came despite continued disruptions in the logistics network in Europe and in the global supply chain, and there remains potential for sales to increase going forward, the company said.
It said sales in September, the first month of its fourth quarter, are expected to increase by 1% in local currencies on year.
H&M cautioned over the summer that its tighter handle on inventory had hit its ability to fully meet demand for some ranges and noted weak consumer confidence in some European markets.
In an update Thursday, Chief Executive Daniel Erver said that heading into autumn the composition of its stock is good, with the company well-placed to meet customer needs.

However, conflict in the Middle East has sent energy prices surging, pushing up inflation and squeezing consumer budgets at the same time as the company grapples with competition from low-cost online platforms such as Shein and Temu as well as its slightly higher-end rival, Zara-owner Inditex.

"At a time when consumers are affected by high living costs, we are gradually strengthening our customer offering through attractive and inspiring products, shopping experiences and brands," Erver said.

H&M reported an operating profit of 6.04 billion Swedish kronor ($608.9 million) for the third quarter through Aug. 31 compared with 4.91 billion kronor a year earlier as reported sales rose 0.3% to 57.19 billion kronor. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected operating profit of 5.52 billion kronor on sales of 57.09 billion kronor.
Operating profit was supported by one-time effects related to tariffs and goods imports that had increased the cost of goods sold in previous quarters, it added.
